```{r setup, echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#code size
def.chunk.hook  <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(
  chunk = function(x, options){
            x <- def.chunk.hook(x, options)
            ifelse(options$size != "normalsize", 
                   paste0("\n \\", options$size,"\n\n", x, "\n\n \\normalsize"), 
                   x)
})
hook_output <- knit_hooks$get("output")
knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
   lines <- options$output.lines
   if (is.null(lines)) {
     return(hook_output(x, options))  # pass to default hook
   }
   x <- unlist(strsplit(x, "\n"))
   more <- "..."
   if (length(lines)==1) {        # first n lines
     if (length(x) > lines) {
       # truncate the output, but add ....
       x <- c(head(x, lines), more)
     }
   } else {
     x <- c(more, x[lines], more)
   }
   # paste these lines together
   x <- paste(c(x, ""), collapse = "\n")
   hook_output(x, options)
 })
```

## Hierarchical occupancy model

Reminder of occupancy model...

Hierarchical model structure:

- one model for estimating where animals really are
- another model for estimating which animals are detected

We estimate the parameters of both models at the same time, using maximum likelihood

```{r, include=FALSE}
# SIMULATE OCCUPANCY DATA #
set.seed(1) # So we all get same data set
M <- 100    # Number of sites
J <- 3      # Number of surveys
beta0 <- -3  # Logit-scale intercept
beta1 <- 0.06  # Slope per percentage point of riparian cover

cover <- sort(round(runif(M, 0, 100), 1))
psi <- plogis(beta0 + beta1 * cover)
z <- rbinom(M, 1, psi)

psi_df <- data.frame(cover = cover,psi=psi,Occupancy=factor(z,levels=c(1,0)))
gpsi <- ggplot(data=psi_df) +
          geom_point(aes(x=cover,y=z,fill=Occupancy,color=Occupancy),
                     position = position_jitter(height=0.05),
                     size=3, shape = 16, alpha=0.4) +
          geom_line(aes(x=cover,y=psi),linewidth=2) + ylab("Pr(occupancy)") + xlab("Riparian cover (%)") +
          theme_bw() + scale_color_fivethirtyeight()
gpsiNL <- ggplot(data=psi_df) +
            geom_point(aes(x=cover,y=z,fill=Occupancy,color=Occupancy),
                       position = position_jitter(height=0.05) , size=3,
                       shape = 16, alpha=0.4) + ylab("Pr(occupancy)") + xlab("Riparian cover (%)") +
            theme_bw() + scale_color_fivethirtyeight() + theme(legend.position = "none")

# SIMULATE DETECTION DATA #
alpha0 <- 1.5                                # Logit-scale intercept
alpha1 <- -0.86                             # Slope per high-flow day
highFlow <- array(round(runif(M * J, 0, 7)), # MxJ high-flow days in preceding week
              dim = c(M, J))                # dimensions: MxJ
p <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * highFlow)         # expected pr(detection)
y <- matrix(NA, nrow = M, ncol = J)         # empty y matrix
for(j in 1:J){
  y[,j] <- rbinom(M, 1, z*p[,j])            # realized y (p*z)
}

# Additional seasons: keep season 1 exactly as simulated above.
# Restore the RNG afterwards so existing jittered figures also stay unchanged.
rng.season1 <- .Random.seed
set.seed(42)
nseasons <- 3
gamma <- 0.20   # gain of site use between seasons
epsilon <- 0.10 # loss of site use between seasons
z.ms <- matrix(NA, nrow=M, ncol=nseasons)
z.ms[, 1] <- z
y.ms <- matrix(NA, nrow=M, ncol=J * nseasons)
flow.ms <- matrix(NA, nrow=M, ncol=J * nseasons)
y.ms[, 1:J] <- y
flow.ms[, 1:J] <- highFlow
for (season in 2:nseasons) {
  previous <- z.ms[, season - 1]
  prob.use <- previous * (1 - epsilon) + (1 - previous) * gamma
  z.ms[, season] <- rbinom(M, 1, prob.use)
  for (visit in 1:J) {
    column <- (season - 1) * J + visit
    flow.ms[, column] <- round(runif(M, 0, 7))
    p.visit <- plogis(alpha0 + alpha1 * flow.ms[, column])
    y.ms[, column] <- rbinom(M, 1, z.ms[, season] * p.visit)
  }
}
season.visit <- paste0("S", rep(1:nseasons, each=J), "V", rep(1:J, nseasons))
colnames(y.ms) <- colnames(flow.ms) <- season.visit
.Random.seed <- rng.season1

p_df <- data.frame(highFlow = c(highFlow),p=c(p),y=c(y),Occasion=c(factor(col(y))),
                   Occupancy = factor(rep(z,3),levels=c(1,0)))
psi_df$Naive <- apply(y,1,max)
gp <- ggplot(data = p_df) +
        geom_point(aes(x=highFlow,y=y, fill=Occupancy,color=Occupancy), position = position_jitter(height=0.05),
                   size=3, shape = 16,  alpha=0.4) +
        geom_line(aes(x=highFlow,y=p),linewidth=1) +
        facet_wrap(.~Occasion)+scale_color_fivethirtyeight() + scale_fill_fivethirtyeight() +
        theme_bw() + ylab("Pr(detection)") + xlab("High-flow days in preceding week")
gpNL <- ggplot(data = p_df) +
          geom_point(aes(x=highFlow,y=y, fill=Occupancy,color=Occupancy), position = position_jitter(height=0.05),
                     size=3, shape = 16, alpha=0.4) +
          facet_wrap(.~Occasion)+scale_color_fivethirtyeight() + scale_fill_fivethirtyeight() +
          theme_bw() + ylab("Pr(detection)") + xlab("High-flow days in preceding week")
gpsiObs <- ggplot(data=psi_df) +
              geom_point(aes(x=cover,y=Naive,fill=Occupancy,color=Occupancy),
                         position = position_jitter(height=0.05) , size=3,
                         shape = 16, alpha=0.4) + ylab("Pr(occupancy)") + xlab("Riparian cover (%)") +
              theme_bw() + scale_color_fivethirtyeight() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Simulate otter transect survey data 

Hypothetical Central Asian otter surveys (all data simulated):

- M=100 fixed 600 m shoreline transects
- J=3 repeat visits within one short season
- occupancy positively related to riparian cover
- detection negatively related to recent high flows 
- true number of occupied sites: `r sum(z)`
- transects with detected signs: `r sum(apply(y,1,max))`

## Simulated otter survey sites

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Schematic network: each segment is one fixed-length river site.
network <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:5, function(branch) {
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 41)
  if (branch == 1) {
    x <- 10 * t
    yy <- 2 + 0.25 * sin(x)
  } else {
    junction <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)[branch - 1]
    side <- c(1, -1, 1, -1)[branch - 1]
    x <- junction + 1.5 * (1 - t)
    yy <- 2 + 0.25 * sin(junction) + side * 3 * (1 - t) +
      0.2 * sin(pi * t)
  }
  data.frame(x = x[-41], yy = yy[-41],
             xend = x[-1], yend = yy[-1])
}))
# Hypothetical habitat coverage, confined to the sampled range.
network$cover <- min(cover) + diff(range(cover)) *
  (rank(network$x + sin(network$yy), ties.method = "first") - 1) /
  (nrow(network) - 1)
# Link the existing simulated survey rows to 100 distinct network sites.
# Spread their locations across the habitat gradient; no new survey data.
survey.rows <- order(network$cover)[round(seq(1, nrow(network), length.out=M))]
network$surveyed <- FALSE
network$surveyed[survey.rows] <- TRUE
network$cover[survey.rows] <- cover
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=3.2, fig.width=8, out.height="2in", warning=FALSE}
ggplot(network) +
  geom_segment(aes(x=x, y=yy, xend=xend, yend=yend,
                   colour=surveyed), linewidth=2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("FALSE"="grey80", "TRUE"="#D11A42"),
                      breaks=c(FALSE, TRUE),
                      labels=c("Not surveyed", "Surveyed"), name=NULL) +
  coord_equal() + theme_void() + theme(legend.position="right")
```

- 100 of 200 hypothetical river segments were surveyed on three visits.
- Each surveyed segment represents a fixed 600 m shoreline transect.

## Otter transect surveys: the inference problem 

Summary of the inference problem (because we don't know truth):

- M=100 fixed 600 m shoreline transects
- J=3 repeat visits within one short season
- \alert{is occupancy related to riparian cover}?
- \alert{is detection related to recent high flows}?  
- \alert{what is the overall occupancy rate}?

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?occu
```

- `formula` is a \alert{double right-hand side formula}
    - first defines the detection model
    - second defines the occupancy model

    - any covariates in the `unmarkedFrameOccu` can be used in the model
    - occupancy can only be modelled using siteCovs


## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit model(s) using the `occu()` function 

- we don't know truth in practice, we have hypotheses
    - about variation in $\psi$
    - about variation in $p$
- potentially a lot of models
- typically want to compare models (eg, using AIC)

## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit model(s) using the `occu()` function 

- we don't know truth in practice, we have hypotheses
    - about variation in $\psi$
    - about variation in $p$
- potentially a lot of models
- typically want to compare models (eg, using AIC)

\vfill

\begin{table}
\begin{tabular}{llll}
\hline
Model & Covariate         & Formula                                                      & \texttt{unmarked} \\ 
\hline
$\psi$    & Null              & $\mbox{logit}(\psi_{i}) = \beta_0$                           & \verb|~1| \\
$\psi$    & Cover (\%) & $\mbox{logit}(\psi_{i}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1\mbox{cover}_{i}$ & \verb|~cover| \\
\hline
$p$       & Null              & $\mbox{logit}(p_{ij}) = \alpha_0$                            & \verb|~1| \\
$p$       & High-flow days              & $\mbox{logit}(p_{ij}) = \alpha_0 + \alpha_1\mbox{highFlow}_{ij}$ & \verb|~highFlow| \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\vfill

## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit model(s) using the `occu()` function 

- we don't know truth in practice, we have hypotheses
    - about variation in $\psi$
    - about variation in $p$
- potentially a lot of models
- typically want to compare models (eg, using AIC)

\vfill

```{r, size="footnotesize"}
# for our simulated data
m1 <- occu(formula = ~1    ~1,     data = umf)
m2 <- occu(formula = ~highFlow ~1,     data = umf)
m3 <- occu(formula = ~1    ~cover, data = umf)
m4 <- occu(formula = ~highFlow ~cover, data = umf) #data generating model
```

\vfill

## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{analyse the results}

Post-fitting analysis steps include:

- which model is preferred? (*model selection*)
- what does the preferred model tell us? (*inference, prediction*)

\vfill

```{r, size="footnotesize"}
# for our simulated data
m1 <- occu(formula = ~1    ~1,     data = umf)
m2 <- occu(formula = ~highFlow ~1,     data = umf)
m3 <- occu(formula = ~1    ~cover, data = umf)
m4 <- occu(formula = ~highFlow ~cover, data = umf)
```


## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{analyse the results}

\alert{Model selection} in `unmarked` using helper functions

- `fitList()` creates a list of fitted occupancy models

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, size="footnotesize",warning=FALSE}
# create a basic fitList (produces warning)
fl <- fitList(m1,m2,m3,m4)

# OR create a NAMED fitList (doesn't produce warning)
fl <- fitList(
  "p(.)    psi(.)"   = m1,
  "p(flow) psi(.)"   = m2,
  "p(.)    psi(cover)" = m3,
  "p(flow) psi(cover)" = m4
)
```


## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{analyse the results}

\alert{Model selection} in `unmarked` using helper functions

- `modSel()` creates a ranked AIC model table from a `fitList` object
    - support for an effect of recent high flows on detection
    - support for an effect of riparian cover on occupancy
    - proceed with AIC-top model

\vfill

```{r, size="footnotesize"}
# create a model selection table
ms <- modSel(fl)
ms
topmod <- m4 # lowest AIC in this simulated dataset
```

\vfill

## Typical `unmarked` workflow - \alert{analyse the results}

\alert{Draw inferences} about occupancy and detection (and modelled relationships)

\vspace{0.5cm}

```{r, echo=FALSE, size="scriptsize"}
topmod@estimates
```

\vspace{0.5cm}

- estimated positive effect of `cover` on occupancy ($\beta_{1} = `r round(coef(topmod)[2],2)` \pm `r round(sqrt(diag(vcov(topmod)))[2],2)`$)
- significant negative effect of `highFlow` on detection ($\alpha_{1} = `r round(coef(topmod)[4],2)` \pm `r round(sqrt(diag(vcov(topmod)))[4],2)`$)

## Now we can make predictions - \alert{in \texttt{unmarked}}

\alert{Draw inferences} about occupancy and detection (and modelled relationships)

- we have estimates (MLEs) of the model parameters ($\beta_{0},\beta_{1},\alpha_{0},\alpha_{1}$)
- possible to calculate $p$ or $\psi$ for any value of riparian cover or recent high-flow days
$$\mbox{logit}(\psi_i) = `r round(coef(topmod)[1], 3)` + `r round(coef(topmod)[2], 3)` \times \mbox{cover}_{i}$$
$$\mbox{logit}(p_{ij}) = `r round(coef(topmod)[3], 3)` + (`r round(coef(topmod)[4], 3)`) \times \mbox{highFlow}_{ij}$$
- use built-in `predict()` function
    - predict detection (`type="det"`)
    - predict occupancy (`type="state"`)
    - provide a data frame of covariate values to make predictions for
    - \alert{must} include covs with identical names to the model 
    
## Now we can make predictions - \alert{in \texttt{unmarked}}

- use built-in `predict()` function
    - predict detection (`type="det"`)
    - predict occupancy (`type="state"`)
    - provide a data frame of covariate values to make predictions for
    - \alert{must} include covs with identical names to the model
- predict the occupancy-cover relationship (`type="state"`):

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, size="footnotesize"}

pred.psi.df <- data.frame(cover = seq(from = min(occdata$cover),
                                   to = max(occdata$cover),
                                   length = 30))
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center',fig.height=3, fig.width=6,out.height="1.8in", warning=FALSE}
glmdf <- data.frame(y = apply(y,1,max), cover = cover)
glmmod <- glm(y ~ cover, data = glmdf, family="binomial")
glmpred <- cbind(pred.psi,glmpred = predict(glmmod,type="response",newdata=pred.psi))
gpsipred1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred.psi, aes(x=cover, ymin=lower, ymax=upper),
              fill="#5B84B1FF", alpha=0.25) +
  geom_line(data = pred.psi, aes(x=cover, y=Predicted), linewidth=2,color="#5B84B1FF") +
  annotate(geom="text", x=75, y=0.2, label="Estimate", color="#5B84B1FF",size=4) +
  ylab("Pr(Occupancy)") + xlab("Riparian cover (%)") + ylim(0,1) + theme_bw()

gppred1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = pred.p, aes(x=highFlow, ymin=lower, ymax=upper),
              fill="#5B84B1FF", alpha=0.25) +
  geom_line(data = pred.p, aes(x=highFlow, y=Predicted), linewidth=2,color="#5B84B1FF") +
  annotate(geom="text", x=5.25, y=0.9, label="Estimate", color="#5B84B1FF",size=4) +
  ylab("Pr(Detection)") + xlab("High-flow days in preceding week") + ylim(0,1) + theme_bw()
plot_grid(gpsipred1,gppred1)
```

\vfill


## Predict otter occupancy across the river network

- Supply riparian cover for every river site, including unsurveyed sites.
- Use the fitted occupancy model (`type="state"`), accounting for imperfect detection.
- Here, 200 hypothetical river sites span the surveyed cover range.



```{r, size="scriptsize"}
network.pred <- predict(topmod, type="state",
                        newdata=network, append=TRUE)
head(network.pred[, c("cover", "Predicted", "lower", "upper")])
```

## Estimated otter occupancy map

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=3.2, fig.width=8, out.height="2in", warning=FALSE}
ggplot(network.pred) +
  geom_segment(aes(x=x, y=yy, xend=xend, yend=yend,
                   colour=Predicted), linewidth=2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(limits=c(0, 1), name="Pr(site use)") +
  coord_equal() + theme_void() + theme(legend.position="right")
```

- Colours show fitted seasonal site-use probabilities, not confirmed presence.
- This is for a **hypothetical** river network in Kyrgyzstan.
- Predictions at unsurveyed sites rely on the fitted relationships.

## Uncertainty in the occupancy map

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.height=3.2, fig.width=8, out.height="2in", warning=FALSE}
network.pred$CIwidth <- network.pred$upper - network.pred$lower
ggplot(network.pred) +
  geom_segment(aes(x=x, y=yy, xend=xend, yend=yend,
                   colour=CIwidth), linewidth=2) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(limits=c(0, 1), name="95% CI width") +
  coord_equal() + theme_void() + theme(legend.position="right")
```

- Wider intervals mean less precise predictions of site use.
- Intervals describe uncertainty conditional on the fitted model.
- Retain probabilities and uncertainty when interpreting a mapped range.

# OPTIONAL: Extension to multi-season (dynamic) occupancy models 

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{data formatting}

Organise observations, site covariates and observation covariates.

- The same 100 sites; three visits in each of three seasons.
- One row per site; visit columns grouped by season then visit.
- `S1V1` = season 1, visit 1; missed visits are `NA`.

```{r, size="scriptsize"}
# combined: detections, cover and high-flow days
msdata <- data.frame(y=y.ms, cover=cover, highFlow=flow.ms)
head(msdata, 2)
```

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{create the unmarkedFrame}

Create an `unmarkedMultFrame` object:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?unmarkedMultFrame
umf.ms <- unmarkedMultFrame(y =          , # observations
                           siteCovs =   , # site covariates
                           obsCovs =    , # visit covariates
                           numPrimary = ) # number of seasons
```

\vspace{0.5cm}

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{create the unmarkedFrame}

Create an `unmarkedMultFrame` object:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?unmarkedMultFrame
umf.ms <- unmarkedMultFrame(y =          , # observations
                           siteCovs =   , # site covariates
                           obsCovs =    , # visit covariates
                           numPrimary = ) # number of seasons
```

- `y` is a binary **M x (J x T)** matrix or data frame.
- Here: 100 sites, three visits, three seasons = **100 x 9**.
- Columns: season 1 visits 1--3, season 2 visits 1--3, then season 3.

\vfill

```{r, echo=FALSE, size="scriptsize"}
head(msdata[, 1:9], 3)
```

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{create the unmarkedFrame}

Create an `unmarkedMultFrame` object:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?unmarkedMultFrame
umf.ms <- unmarkedMultFrame(y =          , # observations
                           siteCovs =   , # site covariates
                           obsCovs =    , # visit covariates
                           numPrimary = ) # number of seasons
```

- `siteCovs` is a data frame with **M** rows.
- Here, riparian cover is a site covariate held constant across seasons.
- Season-varying site covariates would use `yearlySiteCovs`.

\vfill

```{r, echo=FALSE, size="scriptsize"}
head(msdata[, "cover", drop=FALSE], 3)
```

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{create the unmarkedFrame}

Create an `unmarkedMultFrame` object:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?unmarkedMultFrame
umf.ms <- unmarkedMultFrame(y =          , # observations
                           siteCovs =   , # site covariates
                           obsCovs =    , # visit covariates
                           numPrimary = ) # number of seasons
```

- `obsCovs` is a named list of **M x (J x T)** data frames.
- Its columns must match the order of the detection columns in `y`.
- `numPrimary` is the number of seasons: **3**, not the nine visits.

\vfill

```{r, echo=FALSE, size="scriptsize"}
head(msdata[, 11:19], 2)
```

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{create the unmarkedFrame}

Create an `unmarkedMultFrame` object:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, size="footnotesize"}
# for our simulated data
umf.ms <- unmarkedMultFrame(y = msdata[, 1:9],
                           siteCovs = data.frame(cover = msdata$cover),
                           obsCovs = list(highFlow = msdata[, 11:19]),
                           numPrimary = 3)
```

- `y`: nine detection columns, grouped by season then visit.
- `siteCovs`: one row per site.
- `obsCovs`: nine corresponding high-flow columns.
- States are stable within a season; they can change between seasons.

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit a model using the `colext()` function:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?colext
mod.ms <- colext(psiformula =     , # initial occupancy
                 gammaformula =   , # colonisation
                 epsilonformula = , # local extinction
                 pformula =       , # detection
                 data =           ) # an unmarkedMultFrame
```

\vspace{0.5cm}

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit a model using the `colext()` function:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, eval=FALSE, size="footnotesize"}
?colext
mod.ms <- colext(psiformula =     , # initial occupancy
                 gammaformula =   , # colonisation
                 epsilonformula = , # local extinction
                 pformula =       , # detection
                 data =           ) # an unmarkedMultFrame
```

- Four separate formulas, each with a single `~`:
    - `psiformula`: initial probability of site use.
    - `gammaformula`: gain of use at previously unused sites.
    - `epsilonformula`: loss of use at previously used sites.
    - `pformula`: detection probability within each season.
- `data` is an `unmarkedMultFrame` object.

## Multi-season `unmarked` workflow - \alert{model fitting}

Fit a model using the `colext()` function:

\vspace{0.2cm}

```{r, size="footnotesize"}
# for our simulated data
mod.ms <- colext(psiformula = ~cover,
                 gammaformula = ~1,
                 epsilonformula = ~1,
                 pformula = ~highFlow,
                 data = umf.ms)
```

- Initial use is associated with riparian cover.
- Gain and loss probabilities are constant between seasons.
- Detection is associated with recent high flows.

## Interpret changes in otter site use

```{r, include=FALSE}
# Back-transform estimates and intervals to the probability scale.
initial.use <- backTransform(linearComb(mod.ms, c(1, 50), type="psi"))
gain.use <- backTransform(mod.ms, type="col")
loss.use <- backTransform(mod.ms, type="ext")
ms.estimates <- list(initial.use, gain.use, loss.use)
ms.results <- data.frame(
  Process=c("Initial use at 50% cover", "Gain of use (colonisation)",
            "Loss of use (local extinction)"),
  Estimate=vapply(ms.estimates, function(x) unname(coef(x)), numeric(1)),
  Lower=vapply(ms.estimates, function(x) confint(x)[1], numeric(1)),
  Upper=vapply(ms.estimates, function(x) confint(x)[2], numeric(1))
)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, size="scriptsize"}
knitr::kable(ms.results, digits=2, col.names=c("Process", "Estimate", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper"))
```

- Gain is conditional on a site being unused in the previous season.
- Loss is conditional on a site being used; it does not mean an otter died.
- The cover effect describes initial use; later use follows from gains and losses.
- Estimates allow for missed signs; fewer detections alone do not establish loss.
